notes: French read by an English speaker. English borrowed heavily from French, so a great many pairs are identical once accents are folded (nation, table, question). The skeleton folds French accents and the conventions the two spell differently for one sound; -tion, -ique/-ic and -eur/-or fall out of the edit distance without needing rules of their own. Threshold 0.70, the standard, chosen so a pair has to survive both the form and meaning axes rather than looking alike alone. Cutoff 0.80, unchanged by the move to a dictionary-wide map: 5,657 of 23,489 scored surfaces. Set by one word: preservatif scores 0.76 against preservative, so 0.75 would silently remove the most consequential false friend in the language. That single pair is why French sits above the Romance languages it otherwise resembles. Nothing else from the standard list comes close — actuellement 0.23, journee 0.13, monnaie 0.52, raisin 0.15, and assister, blesser and librairie find no match. The deck is a 200-card preview, so the map is calibrated on the whole 50,000-surface frequency list rather than on the deck.
